step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage CMOS operational amplifier with RC Miller compensation in unity-gain follower configuration
step1_figure.description: Figure 24.8 shows the complete schematic of the two-stage op-amp comprising differential input pair M1-M2, current mirror load M3-M4, cascode tail current sink M6T-M6B, common-source second stage M7 with cascode active load M8T-M8B, and Miller compensation network Cc and Rz. The netlist connects the inverting input (gate of M1) to vout and non-inverting input (gate of M2) to vin, forming the closed-loop voltage follower configuration depicted in Figures 24.7, 24.12, and 24.14.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent DC power dissipated by the op-amp and bias generation circuitry

equation.explanation: Sum of all supply currents drawn from VDD multiplied by supply voltage VDD.
equation.assumptions: Quiescent bias conditions with tail current I_M6 = 20 uA, output stage current I_M8 = 10 uA, plus reference bias current from SUB_1.

sky130_expected.calculation: With VDD = 1.8 V, op-amp core draws I_M6 (20 uA) + I_M8 (10 uA) = 30 uA. Bias circuit SUB_1 draws ~30-40 uA. Total supply current ~ 60 uA to 80 uA. P = 1.8 V * 70 uA = 126 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: At 1.8 V VDD with 10-20 uA branch bias currents and the wide-swing cascode bias generator SUB_1, total power is typically around 100-150 uW.

dc_open_loop_gain.description: Low-frequency small-signal open-loop differential voltage gain

equation.explanation: Product of input differential stage gain (gm1 * R1) and second common-source stage gain (gm2 * R2).
equation.assumptions: M1-M4 and M7-M8 operating in active saturation region.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Two-stage amplifier in 130 nm CMOS with cascode loads on stage 1 and stage 2 provides typical open-loop gain between 65 dB and 85 dB.

output_swing_high.description: Maximum output voltage before M7 leaves saturation and enters triode

source.reference: Section 'Output Swing and Current Sourcing/Sinking Capability'

equation.explanation: The maximum output voltage is limited by PMOS driver M7 dropping into triode when V_SD falls below |V_DS,sat|.
equation.assumptions: V_DS,sat,M7 ≈ 100 mV to 150 mV across M7.

sky130_expected.reasoning: With VDD = 1.8 V and typical PMOS overdrive of 100-150 mV, the output reaches within 150 mV of the positive rail.

output_swing_low.description: Minimum output voltage before cascode current sink M8T-M8B enters triode

source.reference: Section 'Output Swing and Current Sourcing/Sinking Capability'

equation.explanation: Output low limit is set by the compliance voltage of the NMOS cascode current sink.
equation.assumptions: Both M8T and M8B require at least V_DS,sat ≈ 100 mV to maintain saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: A wide-swing cascode current sink in SKY130 typically requires 200-300 mV minimum voltage headroom.

current_sinking_capability.description: Maximum output sink current determined by constant current source M8

source.reference: Section 'Output Swing and Current Sourcing/Sinking Capability'

equation.explanation: Because M8 is a constant current sink, the op-amp can only sink up to its DC bias current.
equation.assumptions: M8T and M8B are biased in saturation.

sky130_expected.calculation: I_M8 is nominally designed to be 10 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Direct design parameter fixed by the bias circuit current mirror ratio.

systematic_offset_voltage.description: Input-referred systematic offset voltage resulting from stage sizing mismatch

equation.explanation: The differential input voltage required to drive the output to nominal mid-supply.
equation.assumptions: Balanced layout without random mismatch; systematic sizing M7 vs M4/M3.

sky130_expected.calculation: When properly sized (I_D7 = I_M8), V_OS ≈ 0 V. With slight mismatch, V_OS is within a few millivolts.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Proper current mirroring between input stage and output branch minimizes systematic offset to under 10 mV.

closed_loop_gain.description: Closed-loop DC voltage gain of the follower configuration

equation.explanation: With feedback factor beta = 1 (unity follower), A_CL = A_OL / (1 + A_OL) ≈ 1.

sky130_expected.reasoning: In unity follower configuration with high loop gain, closed loop gain approaches 1 within 0.1%.

dominant_pole_frequency.description: Frequency of the dominant pole created by Miller multiplication of Cc

equation.explanation: Miller effect magnifies Cc at node 1 by approximately gm2 * R2, lowering the pole frequency.
equation.assumptions: Cc = 2.4 pF, gm2 = 140 uA/V, R1 ≈ 500 kOhm, R2 ≈ 500 kOhm.

sky130_expected.reasoning: High stage output resistances combined with 2.4 pF Miller capacitor push the dominant pole into the low kHz range.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Unity gain frequency (gain bandwidth product) of the open-loop op-amp

equation.explanation: Open-loop unity-gain frequency determined by the input pair transconductance and compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Cc = 2.4 pF, dominant pole approximation holds up to f_un.

sky130_expected.calculation: With gm1 ≈ 150 uA/V and Cc = 2.4 pF: f_un = 150e-6 / (2 * pi * 2.4e-12) ≈ 9.95 MHz ≈ 10 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Consistent with Baker's design choice targeting f_un = 10 MHz with Cc = 2.4 pF.

second_pole_frequency.description: Frequency of the non-dominant output pole

equation.explanation: Output node pole after pole splitting.
equation.assumptions: C2 ≈ CL = 100 fF, Cc >> C1, C2.

sky130_expected.calculation: With gm2 ≈ 150 uA/V and CL = 100 fF: f_2 ≈ 150e-6 / (2 * pi * 100e-15) ≈ 238 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: For 100 fF load capacitance and ~150 uA/V stage 2 gm, the non-dominant pole is well above 100 MHz.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin of the loop gain with unity feedback factor

equation.explanation: Difference between loop gain phase at unity gain frequency and -180°.
equation.assumptions: Zero cancelled or pushed to high frequency by Rz; f_un << f_2.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Large ratio of f_2 to f_un (approx 24) results in a highly stable system with phase margin near 90°.

gain_margin.description: Gain margin of the open-loop op-amp

equation.explanation: Attenuation of loop gain magnitude at the frequency where the phase shift reaches -180°.

sky130_expected.calculation: With PM ~ 90° and f_2 >> f_un, the gain at -180° phase is typically -20 dB to -30 dB, giving GM ≈ 20 to 25 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Baker textbook reports GM ≈ 25 dB on page 781 for this compensated design.

settling_time.description: 1% settling time in response to a small 10 mV input step

equation.explanation: For a first-order response with PM ≈ 90°, the closed-loop system time constant tau = 1 / (2*pi*f_un).

sky130_expected.calculation: tau = 1 / (2 * pi * 10 MHz) ≈ 15.9 ns. For 1% settling (approx 4.6 * tau): t_settle ≈ 73 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: As shown in Fig. 24.14, settling occurs within ~70-100 ns after step application.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench measuring DC operating point (power, bias currents), DC transfer characteristics (linear range, output swing, systematic offset), AC frequency response (closed loop gain, bandwidth, stability), and transient small-signal step response (settling time, overshoot) on the Baker Chapter 24 two-stage op-amp.
